newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Conservative Singapore calm on Jackson controversy.
newsitem.headline: Conservative Singapore calm on Jackson controversy.

text.p: Singapore has a reputation for being strait-laced and puritanical, but the city state is playing host to flamboyant pop star Michael Jackson with none of the intolerance shown in other Asian venues.

Recently South Korean civic and religious groups tried unsuccesfully to keep Jackson out, and the Ministry of Culture said the U.S. entertainer had to refrain from making "obscene or vulgar gestures or remarks".
In Malaysia, a concert in Selangor state was blocked by authorities who said he would have an undesirable effect on local youth.
While Singapore stresses conservative social values and has no qualms about censoring what it considers pornographic, it is also trying to become a regional centre for entertainment.
The aim is to boost tourism and the city state's reputation for offering more than clean streets and a low crime rate.
The biggest controversy here surrounding Jackson, who is expected to arrive on Wednesday, is whether ticket prices for his October 25 show are too high for his die-hard fans.
"He is a very good entertainer," said a 24 year-old fan. "But tickets are not cheap. I don't want to pay that much money."
